findings.claim: This diff introduced the leak. own_account_named removes a profile-named own-account debit from M9's operating lines, but the returned direct debit that reverses it is still an operating line: operating_line returns t.reverses is not None for RETURNED_DD, and RETURNED_DD is not in NON_TRADING_IN at line 514. M9 (and M10 and M28) therefore count the reversal as positive operating cash although the debit it undoes is left out. Before this change the two lines netted to zero.
findings.repro: Case profile own_accounts=[ACME HOLDINGS], CMA_RULESET=v2. Statement lines: 'DD ACME HOLDINGS' -300.00, then 'UNPAID DD ACME HOLDINGS' +300.00. The debit is own_account_transfer, rule profile:own_account (debit path; no protected rule matches). The credit is returned_dd by the bank code (protected), and link_reversals sets credit.reverses = debit id (counterparty 'ACME HOLDINGS' on both, same pence). In metrics.compute, operating_line(debit) is False and operating_line(credit) is True, so net_operating rises by £300.00 and M9's evidence cites the returned credit. A fix would also exclude a line whose eff() reverses an own_account_named debit.

findings.claim: Under v1 (frozen path), a profile name is checked after ruleset.protected only, and v1.yaml marks no rule protected. A case-profile name therefore outranks v1's loan_drawdown, loan_repayment, returned_dd and director rules. R54 applies R5 and R6 under v1 (case profile 'new behaviour under any ruleset'), and both requirements say a protected verdict (generic loan wording, a returned payment, a lender) decides first. tests/test_case_profile.py:242-249 asserts the wrong behaviour: M20 = 1160 includes IWOCA and REFUND lines.
findings.repro: CMA_RULESET=v1, directors=[Jane Doe]. Credit 'JANE DOE LOAN' 100.00: v1's loan_drawdown rule matches \bLOAN\b, but classify returns (director_funding, profile:director), so M20 gets the line instead of M21. R5's own example says it is a lending drawdown.

findings.claim: The same v1 precedence gap applies to debits and returned payments. With an own account named, a v1 loan repayment or a returned DD whose wording names that account becomes own_account_transfer. Debt service (M8) then loses the repayment, and M10 and M28 change. R6 requires that a debit to a lender, or a returned direct debit, that names an own account keeps its protected verdict.
findings.repro: CMA_RULESET=v1, own_accounts=[ACME HOLDINGS]. Debit 'DD ACME HOLDINGS LOAN' -100.00 gives (own_account_transfer, profile:own_account), not loan_repayment, so M8 drops by £100. Credit 'UNPAID DD ACME HOLDINGS' 50.00 gives own_account_transfer, not returned_dd.
